metodo.titulo: I build with AI. I direct, design and verify.
metodo.sub: Generation is cheap. What I add is agency, judgment and orchestration.
metodo.agencia.texto: I decide what gets built and what doesn't. I write the brief, the flow and the quality bar before asking for a single line.
metodo.agencia.ejemplo: Fortal: the training rules (double progression, volume by available time, weights you can actually load) were written before the first screen.
metodo.juicio.texto: I review every delivery: I accept it, fix it or have it redone with the reason. I choose between alternatives and document it.
metodo.juicio.ejemplo: coro: I rejected ranking complaints by count and chose to measure concentration; twenty topics with five complaints aren't a defect, one with 47% is.
metodo.orquestacion.texto: I chain agents, tests and full-resolution screenshots. Nothing is done until I've seen it rendered.
metodo.orquestacion.ejemplo: Cathedra: over 6,000 automated tests. Fortal: 746, and every phase verified with 1206×2622 screenshots, one by one.
metodo.confio.titulo: When I trust it and when I redo it
metodo.confio.texto: I trust it when the test passes and the screenshot matches the brief. I redo it when I can't explain the result: if I can't explain it, it doesn't ship. Every case shows one example of each.

marcas.titulo: Three demos with a benefit you can measure.
marcas.sub: Built with the same method as my products. Ámbar Muebles is a fictional brand created for these demos, and so is the club in the bot room. Third-party figures carry their source; the bots figure is my own measurement.
marcas.config.alt: Velvet armchair with walnut wood and brass buttons, in the demo 3D configurator
marcas.config.resuelve: The customer rotates the piece, switches fabric, wood and metal, and sees the price instantly, on a phone and with nothing to install.
marcas.config.gana: Fewer doubts before buying: texture, scale and finish are visible before paying, and "it was not what I expected" goes down.
marcas.config.cifra: Up to twice the conversion on product pages with 3D and augmented reality.
marcas.config.fuente: Threekit, guide to ROI in 3D and AR (Shopify data)
marcas.asis.titulo: A catalogue assistant that does not make things up
marcas.asis.resuelve: It answers pre-sale questions (sizes, lead times, care) citing the product sheet; if the fact is missing, it says so and hands over to a person with a summary.
marcas.asis.gana: Fewer repeated tickets, the same answer for everyone, every answer auditable and service after hours.
marcas.asis.cifra: Average cost in companies that automate; high-volume, rules-based processes pay off the most.
marcas.asis.fuente: Bain & Company, cited by Zapier in its guide to automating a business

caso.cathedra.descripcion: Cathedra, a Windows study app in beta: it transcribes lectures, builds the plan, generates exams and flashcards, and every answer cites the class and the minute. How I defined it, directed it with AI agents and verified it.
caso.cathedra.gancho: From hours of recorded lectures to a study plan where every answer cites the class and the minute.
caso.cathedra.resumen.1: A Windows study app that transcribes lectures and turns that material into the plan, the guides, the exams and the flashcards.
caso.cathedra.resumen.2: University students with recorded lectures and course material.
caso.cathedra.resumen.3: In beta (1.2.0), with a Windows installer and a public page.
caso.cathedra.rol: Founder and product builder. I defined the product, the six-step flow, the identity and the quality bar; I directed development and verified every batch.
caso.cathedra.herramientas: Claude Code (assisted development) · Python · HTML, CSS and JavaScript · local transcription · embedding retrieval
caso.cathedra.cabecera.alt: Cathedra: a class with its steps (guide, questions, cards, mock exam, review) on a glass panel over the desk
caso.cathedra.problema.1: A student piles up hours of recorded lectures and course material, and does not know what the exam covers or where each explanation is.
caso.cathedra.problema.2: Rewatching the whole class does not scale. And a generic assistant answers just as confidently when the fact is not in the material.
caso.cathedra.resultado: Beta 1.2.0 published, with a Windows installer and a public page.
caso.cathedra.apoyo: Full and light installers for Windows 10/11, a security review and legal texts before the beta, over 6,000 automated tests and an admin panel. No users or metrics to report yet.
caso.cathedra.reflexion.1: What I would change: settle the identity before building screens; redoing it twice cost whole batches.
caso.cathedra.reflexion.2: What is missing: with no users yet, I do not know whether a student adopts it unaided. "Record live" is listed as "soon" and is not there.
caso.cathedra.siguiente.alt: Porcelain frame with a screenshot of Fortal
caso.cathedra.galeria.aviso: Screenshots use demo data: fictional subjects, lecturers and student.
caso.cathedra.hace.1: Recorded lectures of up to 4 hours, with an anti-hallucination check; the text is enough to never rewatch the class.
caso.cathedra.hace.2: Classifies every piece of material as content, exam, practical work or course logistics.
caso.cathedra.hace.3: Builds a single study plan from the syllabus calendar; whatever the calendar does not say is flagged.
caso.cathedra.hace.4: A guide per class and per topic, block by block, with the source sentence and minute.
caso.cathedra.hace.5: Mock exams in the format the lecturer announced, calibrated with past exams.
caso.cathedra.hace.6: Mistakes, games and flashcards go into a deck spread out until each exam.
caso.cathedra.hace.7: Explaining the topic in your own words to check you understood it.
caso.cathedra.hace.8: Compares what was covered with the official syllabus and shows what is still missing.
caso.cathedra.hace.9: Every answer carries the class, the minute and who said it; what is not in the material is marked as missing, with an offer to search outside.
caso.cathedra.hace.10: A cloud engine or a four-layer local engine: language, rules, embedding retrieval and symbolic maths.
caso.cathedra.hace.11: Read-aloud and audio summaries: the class in 5 minutes.
caso.cathedra.hace.12: A graphing calculator, 3D concept scenes, memory games and Telegram reminders.
caso.cathedra.decision.1.vi: A student cannot tell a fluent explanation from an invention.
caso.cathedra.decision.1.elegi: Every answer carries the class, the minute and who said it, and the seal stays empty if the fact is not in the material.
caso.cathedra.decision.1.porque: If it cannot be traced back to the lecturer, it is no use for studying.
caso.cathedra.decision.2.vi: In a single class the lecturer mixes content with notes about the exam and the course.
caso.cathedra.decision.2.elegi: Classify every block as content, exam, practical work or course logistics, and build a single plan per subject.
caso.cathedra.decision.2.porque: With several plans you do not know which one to follow; a single one fed by all the material, you do.
caso.cathedra.decision.3.vi: The lectures belong to the student and the connection is not always good.
caso.cathedra.decision.3.elegi: Transcribe and store on the computer, with a local engine that works without internet.
caso.cathedra.decision.3.descarte: Depending only on a cloud service.
caso.cathedra.decision.3.porque: Studying cannot stop because the connection drops.
caso.cathedra.agentes.1: Before asking for a single line I wrote the six steps (start, upload, it reads, ask, sit the exam, review) and the rule that governs them: nothing that is not in the material.
caso.cathedra.agentes.2: Each feature was a batch with a brief, acceptance criteria and mandatory screenshots, and a single agent responsible for it.
caso.cathedra.agentes.3: Before calling anything "final", a separate review checks front and back: copy, buttons and measured contrast in the light theme.
caso.cathedra.agentes.4: Full-resolution screenshots, checked one by one, and over 6,000 automated tests.
caso.cathedra.agentes.5: The identity, twice: the first palette (black and light blue) went and leather, ivory, crystal and cherry stayed; the emblem was redone until the material read as real.

caso.fortal.descripcion: Fortal, an iPhone web app that builds the routine from your real gear and time on a 3D body. Personal app, published and in daily use.
caso.fortal.gancho: A routine built from the gear and the time you actually have, and one I use every day.
caso.fortal.resumen.1: An installable iPhone web app that builds the day’s routine on a 3D model of the body.
caso.fortal.resumen.2: Anyone training with their own gear and little time; today, me.
caso.fortal.resumen.3: Published and in daily use; a personal app, not in the stores.
caso.fortal.rol: Product owner and user. I defined the concept, the look, the sections and the training rules; I directed and verified every phase.
caso.fortal.herramientas: Claude Code · React and TypeScript · Three.js · PWA · IndexedDB · Web Push
caso.fortal.enlace: No public link: single-user app, shown with screenshots
caso.fortal.cabecera.alt: Chest muscle card on the Fortal 3D body: 100 % recovery, rank and sets this week
caso.fortal.problema.1: Gym apps do not know what gear you have at home or how much real time you have per day.
caso.fortal.problema.2: The routine ends up in phone notes and the weights are guessed mid-set.
caso.fortal.resultado: Published and installed on my iPhone; I use it every day.
caso.fortal.apoyo: 746 automated tests. No other users and not in the stores: it is a personal app.
caso.fortal.reflexion.1: What I would change: separate the profile from the code from day one; today it is hard-wired, which is why there is no public link.
caso.fortal.reflexion.2: What is missing: opening it to other people would require accounts and onboarding.
caso.fortal.siguiente.alt: Porcelain frame with a screenshot of AthleteIQ
caso.fortal.hace.1: A body hologram with twenty regions: it marks which muscles are due today and how each one is recovering.
caso.fortal.hace.2.t: A routine for your real time
caso.fortal.hace.2: Builds the week from days, available minutes and intensity, from templates or from scratch.
caso.fortal.hace.3: Computes plates per side, dumbbell dial and weight stack with the gear at hand.
caso.fortal.hace.4: Sets with suggested weight and reps, a rest timer and records on the spot.
caso.fortal.hace.5: Ranks per muscle, estimated 1RM, weekly volume and streak.
caso.fortal.hace.6: A search over about 350 foods, free text ("2 eggs and 150 g of rice") and notifications.
caso.fortal.decision.1.vi: A weight suggestion you cannot load in the gym is noise.
caso.fortal.decision.1.elegi: Compute the weights from the real gear: plates per side, dumbbell dial, weight stack.
caso.fortal.decision.1.descarte: Asking for the weight by hand.
caso.fortal.decision.1.porque: It forces you to do the maths mid-set.
caso.fortal.decision.2.vi: A list of exercises does not show which muscle was left untrained.
caso.fortal.decision.2.elegi: A 3D body with twenty regions painted by what is due today and by recovery.
caso.fortal.decision.2.descarte: A table of sets per muscle.
caso.fortal.decision.2.porque: The body reads at a glance; the table has to be studied.
caso.fortal.decision.3.vi: The only user was me and I wanted to iterate every day.
caso.fortal.decision.3.elegi: A web app installable from Safari, local first and offline.
caso.fortal.decision.3.porque: With no store review and no mandatory server, every change ships the same day.
caso.fortal.agentes.1: The training and nutrition rules (double progression, volume by available time, safety without safety bars) were written before the first screen.
caso.fortal.agentes.2: Gym, routine, live session, food: one phase at a time, each with its brief and measured against those rules.
caso.fortal.agentes.3: A model with twenty muscle regions went through my own pipeline down to a light GLB.
caso.fortal.agentes.4: Screenshots at 1206×2622, the iPhone resolution, checked one by one; 476 unit tests and 270 end-to-end tests as a safety net.
caso.fortal.agentes.5.t: What I removed to show it.
caso.fortal.agentes.5: I pixelated the body data in the screenshots: weight and measurements are not published.

caso.athleteiq.descripcion: AthleteIQ, an AI assistant for sports teams' staff: you ask by chat and it answers with the squad's data. Landing page in five languages with 3D, and chat bots. Working demo.
caso.athleteiq.gancho: The squad, queryable by chat from the field.
caso.athleteiq.resumen.1: An AI assistant for sports teams' staff: you ask by chat and it answers with the squad's data.
caso.athleteiq.resumen.2: Strength coaches and technical staff at professional clubs; the demo is designed for rugby league.
caso.athleteiq.resumen.3: Working demo: a landing page in five languages and test chat bots.
caso.athleteiq.rol: Founder. I defined the concept and the value proposition, wrote the copy in five languages, and directed the design and the build of the bots and the landing page.
caso.athleteiq.herramientas: AI-assisted development · Three.js · Telegram API · HTML, CSS and JavaScript
caso.athleteiq.enlace: Open the demo (generic club, fictional data)
caso.athleteiq.cabecera.alt: AthleteIQ landing page: headline, 3D rugby ball surrounded by metrics in hexagons
caso.athleteiq.problema.1: The technical staff has the data scattered: injury history, training load, session quality, psychological state.
caso.athleteiq.problema.2: They cannot query it in seconds from the field, which is where decisions are made.
caso.athleteiq.resultado: Landing page and bots working as a demo; the landing page opens from this case.
caso.athleteiq.apoyo: No clients or contracts. No return or player figures: they were demo assumptions and are not published.
caso.athleteiq.reflexion.1: What I would change: build it generic from the start; tying it to a real club forced me to sanitise it before I could show it.
caso.athleteiq.reflexion.2: What is missing, and it matters most: validating it with a club.

caso.athleteiq.galeria.aviso: Demo screenshots with a generic club and fictional players.
caso.athleteiq.hace.1: The staff writes the way they talk and gets a reading of the squad data.
caso.athleteiq.hace.2: Questions about injury risk, training load, recovery and squad talent.
caso.athleteiq.hace.3: It accepts voice notes and photos, as well as text.
caso.athleteiq.hace.4.t: In the language of whoever asks
caso.athleteiq.hace.4: The bots answer in the user's language; the landing page comes in five.
caso.athleteiq.hace.5: A real-time 3D rugby ball surrounded by metrics, and a demo chat.
caso.athleteiq.decision.1.vi: The staff decides on the field, phone in hand.
caso.athleteiq.decision.1.elegi: Chat bots that answer in natural language.
caso.athleteiq.decision.1.porque: Nobody opens a dashboard between two drills.
caso.athleteiq.decision.2.vi: An international staff does not work in a single language.
caso.athleteiq.decision.2.elegi: Answer in the language of whoever asks and write the landing page in five (EN, ES, PT, FR, ZH).
caso.athleteiq.decision.2.porque: The question has to come out the way it is thought, untranslated.
caso.athleteiq.decision.3.vi: Without a contract, someone else's name or an assumed figure reads as a promise.
caso.athleteiq.decision.3.elegi: Show the demo with a generic club and fictional players, with no return figures.
caso.athleteiq.decision.3.descarte: Publishing the version tied to a real club.
caso.athleteiq.decision.3.porque: What has not been measured is not shown as a result.
caso.athleteiq.agentes.1: First the message ("The Data Has No Favourites") and the questions the staff would actually ask; then the screens.
caso.athleteiq.agentes.2: Dark, with the 3D ball and the metrics in hexagons; five languages via a dictionary.
caso.athleteiq.agentes.3: They answer by text, voice and photo, in the user's language, about the squad.
caso.athleteiq.agentes.4: Landing page captured at 1920×1080 in every language; bots tested by text, voice and photo.
caso.athleteiq.agentes.5: To publish it I removed the real club, the players, the bot access points and the assumed figures; the demo on this site is that sanitised copy.

caso.coro.descripcion: coro reads a product's public reviews, groups the recurring defect and finds which competitor already fixed it. Prototype with an HTML report.
caso.coro.gancho: From hundreds of reviews to one concrete defect and who already fixed it.
caso.coro.resumen.1: A tool that reads a product's public reviews, groups the recurring defect and looks for which competitor already fixed it.
caso.coro.resumen.2: Whoever buys, sells or manufactures: four profiles read the same report with a different question.
caso.coro.resumen.3: A command-line prototype that generates one HTML report per product.
caso.coro.rol: I defined the product, the profiles, the deciding metric, the rule on solutions and the report format; I directed development and validated it.
caso.coro.herramientas: AI-assisted development · Node.js · ES modules · static HTML report
caso.coro.cabecera.alt: coro report: header, verdict and four metrics of the test product
caso.coro.problema.1: A thousand negative reviews spread over twenty topics are noise; a hundred saying the same thing is a fixable defect.
caso.coro.problema.2: Whoever buys, sells or manufactures has no time to read them and does not know whether someone already solved it.
caso.coro.resultado: A command-line prototype that generates the HTML report for a product.
caso.coro.apoyo: It runs on a product's reviews or on a local test set. No users or clients.
caso.coro.reflexion.1: What I would change: publish a sample report as a page from the start; today there are only screenshots.
caso.coro.reflexion.2: What is missing: it runs from the command line, so a brand cannot use it on its own yet.
caso.coro.siguiente.alt: Porcelain frame with a screenshot of Cathedra
caso.coro.galeria.aviso: Screenshots of the test fixture; suppliers and sources replaced with generic names.
caso.coro.hace.1: A product's public reviews: 400 in the largest real run and 1,200 in a load test.
caso.coro.hace.2: Groups topics and computes what share of the negatives point at the same thing, by severity and with a surcharge if it grows.
caso.coro.hace.3: Every topic brings quotes with date and stars.
caso.coro.hace.4: Root-cause hypothesis and estimated impact per topic.
caso.coro.hace.5: Solutions with a source; if there is no evidence, the report says so.
caso.coro.hace.6: Consumer, entrepreneur, brand buying from a third party and brand that manufactures.
caso.coro.decision.1.vi: Twenty topics with five complaints are not a defect; one with 47 % is.
caso.coro.decision.1.elegi: Measure concentration: what share of the negatives points at the same thing.
caso.coro.decision.1.porque: Counting rewards the most talked-about topic, not the defect that keeps coming back.
caso.coro.decision.2.vi: An invented solution reads as confidently as a real one.
caso.coro.decision.2.elegi: Solutions are searched for and cited with a source, and the report says when there is no evidence.
caso.coro.decision.2.porque: A "not found" is worth more than an invented solution.
caso.coro.decision.3.vi: The same complaint asks different things of whoever buys and whoever manufactures.
caso.coro.decision.3.elegi: One report with four readings: consumer, entrepreneur, brand buying from a third party and brand that manufactures.
caso.coro.decision.3.porque: "Should I buy it?" and "what do I claim from my supplier?" are not answered by the same paragraph.
caso.coro.agentes.1: The profiles and the metric were defined before the code: concentration, by severity, with a surcharge if the topic grows.
caso.coro.agentes.2: Analysis, quality, history, profiles, solutions and report, each with its acceptance criteria.

saber.titulo: Eight areas, each with the project where I used it.
saber.sub: Each tag links to the case study. "Internal" is my own work that I do not publish; "client" is work for a third party I do not name.
saber.deslizar: Swipe to see all eight areas →
saber.1.1: A watcher that spots a new recorded lecture, transcribes it, files it under its subject and archives it.
saber.1.2: A connector that downloads lecture recordings from Teams on its own.
saber.1.3: Releasing a version in one command, with a guard that stops if it finds keys or personal paths.
saber.1.4: A Windows installer in two editions: full and light.
saber.1.5: Loading sources into NotebookLM notebooks with deduplication and content checks: 358 sources loaded.
saber.1.6: A review analyser that validates the sample before spending on the analysis.
saber.2.1: A Telegram bot that answers text, photos and transcribed voice notes, with per-chat history and a usage limit.
saber.2.2: Reminders for exams and deadlines, generated from the course calendar.
saber.2.3: A prototype daily brief of industry news and an opportunity radar that drops repeats, both scheduled.
saber.2.4: Workout push notifications on the iPhone.
saber.2.6: Incoming messages with deduplication and caching, in Apps Script.
saber.3.1: Local transcription of lectures up to 4 hours long, with the model chosen by measuring on my own graphics card.
saber.3.2: Local language engine, embedding retrieval and synthetic voice, all offline.
saber.3.3: Answers that cite the class and the minute; whatever is not in the material is flagged as missing, never made up.
saber.3.4: Exams, flashcards and games generated from the material, and a simulated student who studies for a week to measure quality.
saber.3.5: Splitting the work between models by cost and quality.
saber.3.6: A fraud-detection agent with logistic regression: 83.3% accuracy against 33.3% and 66.7% for the baselines; graded 10/10.
saber.4.1: A local server with Origin checks and path traversal defence: listening only on your own machine is not enough.
saber.4.2: CSP and passwords hashed with scrypt and salt, with an attempt cap and atomic writes.
saber.4.3: Codes stored as hashes with a per-minute limit, and the user's key encrypted with DPAPI.
saber.4.4: Proxies without SSRF, a size cap and a required credential on every route, with tests.
saber.4.5: Legal and privacy research before the beta: terms, AI notice and which data leaves the device.
saber.5.1: A complete brand identity: leather, ivory, glass and cherry, with a layered 3D emblem.
saber.5.2: 23 Blender scripts rendering backgrounds, icons and atlases in Cycles, with PBR materials and real textures.
saber.5.3: Liquid glass with refraction, and light and dark themes with contrast measured on pixels.
saber.5.4: A hologram shader with bloom and a 3D body with labelled muscles.
saber.5.6: Sound signatures mastered to −18 LUFS, and reduced motion respected.
saber.6.1: A desktop app with WebView2 and a local server with streaming.
saber.6.2: A local-first PWA that works offline, with Web Push and Workbox, in React 19 and TypeScript.
saber.6.3: A two-sided marketplace in production: Next.js, Postgres with 27 migrations, accounts, messaging and contracts.
saber.6.4: A 3D landing page in five languages.
saber.6.5: Exporting a store mock-up with 3D to Shopify.
saber.6.6: Deployments on Vercel, Cloudflare and Netlify.
saber.7.1: Postgres with migrations and seed data.
saber.7.2: Logistic regression with leave-one-out validation and baselines.
saber.7.3: Backtests and simulation without look-ahead bias, with news stored at the real time it arrived: 543 queries with measured cost.
saber.7.4: Connections to exchanges and prediction markets.
saber.7.6: A graphing tool and symbolic algebra.
saber.8.1: A 189-item board with status and evidence, and a roadmap in 4 phases.
saber.8.2: Batches of AI agents with a brief and acceptance criteria, and an independent review of every delivery.
saber.8.3: Verification with full-resolution screenshots before calling anything done.
saber.8.4: Test suites: over 5,500 passing in Cathedra; 391 unit, 85 server and 270 end-to-end in Fortal.
saber.8.5: Performance measurement: milliseconds per frame and memory.
saber.8.6: Pricing by plan, cost studies and e-commerce unit economics.
